title: Data Type Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Type a value or pick a robot value and watch it slide into the int, float, str, or bool bin, with a REPL-style type() check and a plain-English reason.

educational.topic: MicroPython data types: int, float, str, bool
learningObjectives: Classify a value as int, float, str, or bool
Explain how a decimal point, quotes, or a capital letter changes a value's type
Recognize values that cause NameError or SyntaxError
Predict which types can be used in math such as value + 1
prerequisites: Variables and assignment (Chapter 3: Variables and Assignment)
The four core data types (Chapter 3: The Four Core Data Types)

simulationModel.modelType: Rule-based literal classifier matching Python syntax
assumptions: Digits only (optional minus) is int; digits with one decimal point is float
Text in matching single or double quotes is str; exactly True or False is bool
Other words are variable names (NameError); anything else is a SyntaxError
limitations: Scientific notation, lists, and other types are not covered
Error messages follow MicroPython wording, which differs slightly from desktop Python

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Type or pick a value, optional bin prediction, animated sort, REPL-style explanation
keyQuestions: What is the one feature that makes 15.0 a float instead of an int?
Why is "15" a string even though it looks like a number?
Why does true cause an error but True does not?
Which types can you add 1 to?
commonMisconceptions: A value's type depends on what it means, not how it is written
Numbers in quotes can still be used in math
true and True are the same in Python
assessmentOpportunities: Prediction tally for the ten robot values
Challenge: 0.92 float, "65535" str, False bool, 20 int
Exit ticket about a sensor value that arrives as text
